newsitem.title: YEMEN: Italian tourist abducted in Yemen released.
newsitem.headline: Italian tourist abducted in Yemen released.

text.p: An Italian tourist kidnapped by Yemeni tribesmen has been released, an Italian diplomat in Sanaa said on Sunday.
"Giorgio Bonanomi was released at 2100 local time (1800 GMT)," Simonetta Bartolomei, charge d'affairs at the Italian embassy in Sanaa told Reuters.
"He is in goood health, and he is free to stay or return to Italy," she said adding that Yemeni authorities negotiated the release.
Bonanomi, 49, was abducted on Wednesday. A Yemeni security official said he was taken to Radaa in al-Baidha province, 150 km (93 miles) southeast of the capital Sanaa.
Bonanomi, from Lecco in northern Italy, was kidnapped less than two weeks after the abduction of two other Italians by Yemeni tribesmen.
Luigi Archetti and Maria Paola Mariconi were held as part of a property dispute with authorities but were released after one day.
Kidnapping is a common tactic by Yemeni tribes holding grievances against the government or foreign oil firms operating in Yemen, one of the Arab world's poorest countries.

Tribesmen have tried to use hostages -- who have included French and U.S. diplomats and a Saudi ambassador -- as bargaining chips in mostly land and water disputes. All hostages have been released unharmed so far.
